# Contributing

Bug reports, design feedback, documentation improvements, and focused pull
requests are welcome.

Most of Atelier's code was generated by AI without a complete line-by-line maintainer review. Expect sharp edges and
breaking changes. Contributions should therefore be small enough to review
carefully and should include evidence for the behavior they change.

## Before opening a pull request

- Open an issue first for new tools, public API changes, dependencies, storage
  formats, or broad refactors.
- Keep unrelated cleanup out of the change.
- Never create or push a release tag. Releases are maintainer-only.

## Development setup

Install the Rust toolchain declared in `rust-toolchain.toml`, clone the
repository, and run:

```sh
make check
```

The supported native development and release environment is Ubuntu 22.04 or
newer on x86_64. The supported container target is Alpine linux/amd64.

That non-mutating gate checks release metadata, formatting, Clippy, rustdoc,
tests, and tool-reference rendering.

Useful commands:

```sh
make fmt          # apply formatting
make test         # complete Rust test suite
make docs         # generate target/atelier-tools.html
make release      # optimized binary
```

The workspace commits `Cargo.lock` because it publishes executable artifacts.
Include its changes when adding or updating dependencies.
Rust 1.88 remains the minimum supported compiler and has a dedicated CI check.

The hooks in `.githooks/` are optional:

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

CI is authoritative even when the hooks are enabled.

## Pull requests

A good pull request:

- explains the user-visible problem and the chosen scope;
- links the issue for non-trivial changes;
- adds or updates tests for behavior changes;
- updates the changelog when users will notice the change;
- keeps the generated tool reference working when the tool surface changes;
- passes every required CI check.

Maintainers may ask to split a pull request when independent changes would be
easier to review separately. Pull requests are squash-merged.

## Security

Do not report vulnerabilities in a public issue. Follow
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to disclose them privately.
